items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Kernels are full of cryptic names (`ru0..ru3`, `rv0..rv3`, `r_sum`) and bare literals such as `8414 * r0 + 16519 * g0 + 3208 * b0 + 524544) >> 9` and `8389120) >> 10`. Neither the names nor the constants are tied to their FFmpeg counterparts. Layout and formatting are otherwise consistent.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: `process_rgb24_to_nv12` and `process_rgb24_to_nv21` are near-identical copies, each over 100 lines with three copy-pasted vertical-filter branches. `unscaled.zig` is 52KB, far over 500 lines. The diff commits `.zig-cache/` and `zig-out/lib/libswscale_candidate.so` build artifacts.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Magic constants are everywhere (`1 << 17`, `2048`, `1536`, `512`, RGB coefficients). `swscale_process` heap-allocates scratch buffers on every call (`ctx.allocator.alloc(i32, ctx.src_h * chr_w)`). Odd widths and heights are not validated, so the paired-pixel loop reads past the end of the row.

items.name: Geometry, stride and tail handling
items.name_zh: 几何尺寸、步长与尾部处理
items.evidence: `while (x < ctx.src_w) : (x += 2)` reads `s_row[(x+1)*3]`, which goes out of bounds on odd widths. The `cy == 0` branch reads `u_rows[2*chr_w..3*chr_w]`, so a 2-pixel-tall frame reads past the buffer. The scalar kernels shown have no SIMD, and nothing checks for unsupported geometry.

items.name: ABI and build-target conformance
items.name_zh: ABI 与构建目标符合要求
items.evidence: The library comes from the scaffold's build.zig (x86-64-v3) and the C-ABI process functions return 0 or -1, so the ABI looks correct. However, per-call scratch allocation happens in `swscale_process` instead of being precomputed in `swscale_create`.
